text:
- chief complaint: the patient presents with a nonhealing ulcer on the right foot, present for about six to eight weeks.
- history of present illness: the patient reports a painless right lateral foot ulcer, possibly worsening since first noticed, that may have followed minor trauma while doing yard work. The patient has type 2 diabetes on insulin with recent glucose readings above normal and an A1c above 9. History includes a 2018 heart attack with right coronary stent, and a former smoker of at least two packs per day for over 20 years, quit about four years ago.
- physical examination: afebrile, blood pressure 127/80, heart rate in the 60s. No jugular venous distention or carotid bruits. Clear lungs. 2/6 systolic ejection murmur at the left base. Absent dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses palpated. 2 x 3 cm ulcerated lesion on the right lateral foot near the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint, with granulation tissue, slight purulent discharge, no cellulitis, and no tenderness.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: intermittent numbness and tingling in the feet, worse in cold weather; chronic tension headaches; no fever, chills, chest pain, shortness of breath, or calf pain with walking.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: N/A.
- follow-up instructions: arterial ultrasound of the lower extremities, podiatry consult for wound care, coordination with the primary care physician for diabetes control, continue aspirin and statin, and cardiology input on procedural clearance.
